name: LEAPS Long Call
summary: Buy a call with more than a year to expiry, usually 0.70-0.80 delta, as a multi-quarter leveraged long or as the anchor leg for later call overwriting.
max_loss: Debit paid x 100. Can still be a 100% loss over a 2-year horizon.
breakevens: strike + debit per share at expiry; much lower on a mark-to-market basis

greeks.theta: very small per day (< 0.15% of debit/day) but total extrinsic is large in dollars
greeks.vega: large positive - LEAPS are the most vega-sensitive long single options in dollar terms

when_to_use: IVR < 25 on a name with a multi-quarter thesis. Vega dominates: buying LEAPS in a high-IV regime is the single most expensive long-premium mistake available.
entry_rules: IVR < 25 - hard gate. LEAPS are a long-vega position first and a directional position second
Debit <= 8% of equity (~$4,000 on $50k) per name; max 3 LEAPS positions at once
Underlying must be a liquid large cap or major ETF - no LEAPS on illiquid single names
management_rules: Take profit at +100% of debit, or roll up (sell, buy a higher strike at 0.70-0.80 delta) to bank half the gain
Roll out when DTE < 180: extrinsic decay accelerates and the leverage story degrades
Stop at -40% of debit or a monthly close below the 200-day SMA
If IVR rises above 70 with the position profitable, sell to close or roll up - realise the vega
exit_rules: Close at +100%, -40%, or when DTE < 180 (roll or exit)
Never hold into the final month. Flatten or roll with >= 30 DTE remaining to avoid auto-exercise into 100 shares
assignment_risk: None (long). Exercise risk at expiry only, and the share purchase would be large - the 30-DTE roll rule prevents it.
liquidity_needs: LEAPS markets are wide. Trade only underlyings with LEAPS OI >= 100 and mid-based fills achievable.
common_mistakes: Buying LEAPS at high IV rank; using them as set-and-forget with no roll discipline; selling short calls against them without approval for the resulting diagonal (that is a spread, not this strategy).
